transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. Am I okay to just sit here? Okay, great. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I don't want to sound dramatic or anything, I know you see people with much worse problems. But I've just been having a hard time with some thoughts lately, and my family thought I should talk to someone. 

I've been an electrician for a lot of years, and... well, if all my experience couldn't keep my own brother safe, then... I just, I can't shake the thought that I'm a danger to anybody who works with me. Or even the people living under my roof. I know that probably sounds awful, I'm sorry to just dump that on you right away. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Can you tell me more about these thoughts? Are they intrusive or unwanted, and do they keep coming back to you even if you try to ignore them?

Yeah... um, yes, Doctor. I try really hard to ignore them, I promise I do. I don't want to make a big deal out of it or let it affect my work, but... they do just keep coming back. I hope I'm explaining this right. 

Like, I'll just be in the middle of a totally normal day, maybe wiring a panel at a job, or... or even just at home hearing my nephew shut the garage door. And then, I don't know, it's like the whole job site or the room just drops out from under me. Suddenly I'm right back there, smelling the smoke, and... and seeing my brother. 

I know that sounds completely crazy, and I'm really sorry if I'm not making sense. I try to just shake it off so I don't bother anyone with it, but it's hard. Is... does that sound like what you were asking about? I hope that's the right kind of answer.

Can you tell me more about those moments when you feel like you’re right back at the scene with your brother—how often do those happen, and do they feel like flashbacks or vivid memories that come on their own?

Um, yeah, I guess they do feel a bit like... like flashbacks, maybe? I don't want to use the wrong word, but it's like I'm really there for a second. 

As for how often... well, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I mean, I'm still functioning, mostly. I'm trying really hard to keep it together. But... I guess it happens a few times a week. Sometimes more if it's a stressful week. I try my best to just push through it so I don't mess up anyone else's day, you know? 

I hope that's not too weird or... or crazy sounding. I know you must hear all kinds of things. Is that... is that the kind of information you need? I can try to explain it better if I didn't do a good job.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened to your brother?

Well... um, I guess maybe a little bit? I try really hard not to let it get in the way of normal life, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just hiding away or anything. But... yeah, I suppose there are a few things. 

Like, I don't really go out into my own garage much anymore. Unless I absolutely have to, I mean! I still grab things if we really need them, I'm not completely avoiding my own house. But I try to stay out of there if I can help it. 

And, um... I actually quit helping out with the electrical maintenance at our church. I just told them I was taking a break because work was busy. I didn't want to make a big scene or make them feel bad, but I just couldn't bring myself to do it anymore. 

Also... if people start talking about car projects, or... or the fire... I tend to shut the conversation down pretty fast. I know it's probably rude of me, and I feel awful for being short with people, I really do. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a jerk. It's just easier to change the subject, you know? 

Am I... is that the kind of thing you mean, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or thoughts since the incident with your brother, like feeling guilty, blaming yourself, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Well... um, yeah, I guess my mood has been a little off. I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party, because I know people go through worse things. I really try to keep a positive attitude for my family. 

But... um... the truth is, I've been having some really hard thoughts. I guess that's actually the main reason I finally came in to see you. I hope it's okay to admit this, but... I just can't shake this feeling that I'm... I'm a danger to people. 

I mean, I've been an electrician for years, right? I know what I'm doing. But if all that experience couldn't keep my own brother safe... then how can I trust myself? I just keep thinking that I'm a danger to anyone who works with me on a job site, or... or even the people who live under my roof. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm being too hard on myself, and I'm sorry to lay all that on you. I try not to let it show because I don't want my wife to worry. Do you... do you think it's normal to feel that way after something like this? I just hope I'm not totally losing my mind.
Have you been feeling guilty or blamed yourself for what happened to your brother, even if it wasn’t your fault?

Um, well... I try really hard not to dwell on it, because I know I need to be strong for everyone. I don't want to sound ungrateful that I'm still here, you know? But... yeah, I guess I do blame myself a lot. 

There's just this... this really heavy mix of guilt and, honestly, some anger just sitting in my chest all day. I try to hide it, I promise I don't take it out on anyone. It just gets really hard when... when I look at my nephew. I look at him and I just think about how he lost his dad, and... and now he got stuck with me instead. 

I feel terrible even saying that out loud. I hope you don't think I'm a bad uncle or a bad person for feeling that way. I'm trying my best to step up for him and be helpful. Is it... is it normal to feel that kind of guilt all the time? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers, I hope I'm not overcomplicating things.
Have you noticed that these feelings of guilt or anger tend to linger most days, even when you're not thinking about the incident directly?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say they linger *all* the time. I really try my best to keep busy, you know? I want to make sure I'm still pulling my weight at work and at home, so I don't just sit around dwelling on things. I try to keep a smile on my face for my wife and my nephew. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I feel a little down, but I wouldn't want you to think I'm just walking around angry all day. I promise I'm not a grumpy person to be around! I try really hard to be pleasant and helpful. 

So, um... no, I don't think I'd say those feelings are there most days when I'm not thinking about it. I hope that's okay? I just want to be honest with you, but I also don't want to make things sound worse than they actually are. Is that the kind of thing you were asking, Doctor?
Have you found yourself not caring about things that used to be important to you, or feeling emotionally numb, like you're just going through the motions?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm numb or anything like that. I still care about things, really I do. I mean, I still show up for work every day, and I make sure the bills are paid and the house is taken care of. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or neglecting my responsibilities. 

I guess... maybe I don't get as excited about things as I used to? Like, I used to love tinkering with old radios in the garage on the weekends, but lately I just... I haven't really felt the urge to go out there. But I think that's just because I've been trying to spend more time inside, making sure my wife and nephew have what they need. I'm just trying to be helpful, you know?

So, I'm definitely not just going through the motions. I'm still very involved, I promise. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want to sound like I've stopped caring about my family or my life. Is that an okay answer?
Have you noticed that you feel down, irritable, or emotionally upset most days, even when nothing specific is happening to cause those feelings?

Um, well... I really try my best not to let things get me down, you know? I mean, I have a good life, a good job, and I know I have a lot to be thankful for. I wouldn't want to sound like a complainer or someone who just mopes around all day for no reason. 

I guess... sometimes I might feel a little tired or stressed, but I think that's just normal for anyone working full time and trying to help out with family, right? I really try to keep a positive attitude, especially around my wife and my nephew. I don't want to bring down the mood in the house or make them feel bad. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I feel upset or irritable most days. I try very hard to be patient and easygoing. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of how I'm doing, without sounding like I'm making a big deal out of nothing. Is that okay?
Have you noticed yourself feeling more on edge, easily startled, or having trouble sleeping since the incident with your brother?

Um, well... I really try not to let things get to me, you know? I want to be well-rested so I can do a good job at work and be present for my family. I don't want to be one of those guys who's always jumpy or complaining about being tired. 

I mean... I guess sleeping has been a little bit tricky lately, but I'm sure it's nothing major. It's just... well, most nights I end up just lying there, kind of listening. Like, I'll be listening for any weird crackling sounds, or for a car door to shut in the driveway. Just making sure everything is safe, you know? Being responsible. 

And, um... when I do manage to drift off, sometimes I'll wake up kind of suddenly. Like a jolt. And I'll be all sweaty, usually from these dreams about the garage. Then it's just... hard to settle back down before my alarm goes off for work. But I still make it to work on time! I don't let it interfere with my job. 

I hope it's alright that I mentioned that? I really don't want to sound like I'm falling apart or anything. I'm still keeping it together. Does that make sense, Doctor?
